newsitem.title: JAMAICA: Layoffs planned for Jamaica bauxite industry.
newsitem.headline: Layoffs planned for Jamaica bauxite industry.

text.p: Low world prices for aluminium are forcing two of Jamaica's four bauxite mining firms to shed a total of 350 jobs within the next few weeks, industry officials said on Wednesday.

Alcan Jamaica, subsidiary of Canadian-based Alcan Aluminium Ltd, will lay off 270 workers employed at its Kirkvine and Ewarton plants, as well as the Port Esquivel facility. A company spokesman said the layoffs were in line with a restructuring being carried out by Alcan worldwide.
Alumina Partners (Alpart), a joint venture between the Jamaican government, Kaiser Aluminum and Norsk Hydro, is expected to lay off 80 workers, mostly clerical and administrative workers.

Low world prices for aluminium were cited as a major factor behind the staff cuts. For the first nine months of 1996, total crude bauxite shipments rose 9.8 percent, from 2.69 million metric tons to 2.96 million tons. Total alumina shipments climbed 8.9 percent, from 2.25 million to 2.45 million tons.

However, gross earnings for the first six months of the year declined 4.3 percent, from US$353.4 million in 1995 to US$338.1 million, and officials said they expect the trend will continue for the rest of the year.
